BloodDome99, developed and published by Halftone Gaming, is a frantic arena shooter that blends twin-stick action with roguelite progression, all wrapped in a satirical, dystopian game show premise. It presents a world where survival is entertainment and contestants are thrown into a brutal spectacle for the amusement of unseen audiences. While the narrative elements remain largely in the background, they provide enough flavor to give context to the relentless combat, turning what could have been a purely mechanical experience into something with a bit more personality.

The gameplay is built around surviving waves of enemies in confined arenas, where movement and positioning are just as important as firepower. Players control their character with responsive twin-stick controls, weaving through incoming attacks while unleashing a constant stream of damage. The pacing is immediate and unforgiving, with little downtime between encounters. Each run escalates quickly, pushing players to adapt to increasing chaos as enemy numbers grow and attack patterns become more complex. This creates a constant sense of pressure that defines the core experience.

What adds depth to this structure is the roguelite progression system. As players fight through waves, they collect currency and upgrades that shape their build for that run. The game offers a wide selection of weapons and perks, allowing for a range of playstyles. Some combinations focus on raw damage output, while others emphasize survivability or crowd control. This flexibility encourages experimentation, as different builds can dramatically change how a run unfolds. The ability to carry multiple weapons at once further expands this system, creating opportunities for synergy and strategic layering.

A notable aspect of the game is how it handles resource management within each run. Players must decide whether to spend their earnings on immediate upgrades or save toward long-term objectives, such as progressing further or unlocking escape conditions. This introduces a subtle but meaningful layer of decision-making, adding tension beyond the moment-to-moment combat. It is not just about surviving the next wave, but about managing resources in a way that supports overall progress.

The visual presentation leans heavily into a retro-inspired aesthetic, combining pixel art with neon highlights to create a vibrant, chaotic atmosphere. The arenas are filled with exaggerated effects, from explosive weapon impacts to swarms of enemies, all designed to keep the action visually engaging. The soundtrack complements this with energetic, fast-paced tracks that reinforce the intensity of the gameplay. Together, these elements create a cohesive style that feels both nostalgic and modern.

Despite its strengths, the game does have limitations that become more noticeable over time. The core loop, while highly engaging in short bursts, does not change significantly as players progress. Runs follow a similar structure, and while the variety of weapons and upgrades adds some diversity, the overall experience can begin to feel repetitive during longer sessions. Balance can also be uneven, with certain builds proving far more effective than others, which may reduce the incentive to experiment once optimal strategies are discovered.

The difficulty curve is another defining feature. The game quickly ramps up the challenge, requiring fast reflexes and constant awareness. For players familiar with the genre, this creates a satisfying test of skill, but it can be overwhelming for newcomers. The lack of a more gradual introduction means that early failures are common, though the quick restart loop helps maintain momentum and encourages repeated attempts.

Ultimately, BloodDome99 succeeds in delivering a focused and energetic experience that captures the essence of arcade-style shooters while incorporating modern progression systems. It does not attempt to expand beyond its core idea, instead refining it into a tight, replayable loop that emphasizes action and adaptability. Its strengths lie in its pacing, customization, and visual identity, even if its structure remains relatively narrow.

In the end, it stands as an engaging and well-executed entry in the arena shooter space, offering fast, chaotic gameplay that rewards persistence and experimentation. While it may not sustain long-term variety for every player, it provides a consistently entertaining experience for those who enjoy skill-driven, repeatable challenges.

[h1]THIS DOME'S A KEEPER[/h1]
[i]Eh? Eh? See what I did there?[/i]

[b]BloodDome99 = The Running Man + Tandy Home Computer + Vampire Surviors[/b]

Yes, yes, the survivors/bullet-heaven genre is heavily over-saturated with scores of mediocre takes littering the store... However this genre is one of my absolute favorite guilty pleasures. For my part, these games hearken back to arcade classics like Robotron in much the same way that many twin-stick shooters do and it's a vibe I still enjoy.

Does Blood Dome 99 innovate on this formula? Eh... Not terribly. However, it doesn't need to. It's a game that plays to it's strengths and DGAF about it's weaknesses. It's strengths lie in just how quick and easy it is to get straight into the action, the simple but highly stylish graphics, the (mostly) satisfying feel and capturing that 80s retrofuture dystopia theme perfectly.

Honestly, what sets it apart from me is that the runs are FAST. In Vampire Survivors, Halls of Torment, and other similar giants of the genre, once you get rolling you can spend 30 minutes - 1 hour on some levels and they just begin to drag. Sometimes, a lot times, all I want is a game that is extremely sessionable. 15 - 30 minutes tops, nobody is overstaying their welcome and making things awkward like your weird uncle at Thanksgiving. This is where Blood Dome delivers.

[i]Take one to the dome if you...[/i]

[list]
[*] 🩸Want a game that does what it sets out to do and does it hard and fast (oh my)
[*] 🩸Get warm nostalgia for classic 80s quasi-futuristic dystopias that certainly won't now fill you with existential dread... Ha... Ha...
[*] 🩸Are a bullet-heaven junky that just needs a fix, just a few rounds man, you're good for it, man, PLEASE, PLEASE, man!
[/list]

[i]Get running, man, if you...[/i]

[list]
[*] 🏃Are burnt out on survivor-likes, I mean, you probably aren't even on this page if that's the case though.
[*] 🏃Are averse to retro-themes and goofy, over-the-top presentation and humor
[*] 🏃Tend to calculate whether a game is "worth it" based solely on the sheer number of hours per dollar ratio
[/list]

[h3][u]The Bottom Line[/u][/h3]

Is the Blood Dome the Best Dome? No, but it is far from the Worst Dome. That dubious honor belongs to 1996's Bio-Dome starring Pauly Shore and Stephen Baldwin.

BloodDome99 is one of the most interesting survivors-like games that I have played.

Your goal is freedom, and to achieve this, you need to collect $300,000 and defeat the boss. 

Killing enemies grants you money and drops XP orbs. Money is the most crucial part of the game. Aside from summoning the boss, money is used to buy abilities when you level up. Upon leveling up, you are offered a choice of one of three abilities, each with a different cost. You can also skip the abilities and receive money instead. 

The game doesn't feature traditional meta-progression. Instead, it allows players to buy guns and perks that can appear as abilities during level-ups in subsequent runs. You can purchase them in the main menu at the vending machine. Besides guns and perks, you can also buy soundtracks and cosmetics. 

The game is fun and features nice Synthwave/Retrowave visuals and music styles. Definitely worth to check it.

tl;dr: Yes, but as long as you're OK with a pretty simple, short, semi-novel take on a bullet heaven. 

The arguably most interesting thing in BloodDome99 is the dynamic between levels and money. You get money automatically by killing enemies, but you have to pick up their XP to level. When you level, your funds determine what possible perks you can afford (also weapons, which drop in via drone every so often during a run). When you hit 300k of funds, the boss spawns, and killing the boss ends the run. So maximizing XP you pick up, and spending on the biggest things you can, will give you more power, at the cost of a longer run (there is a scoreboard for that, but TBH it's pretty pointless right now due to the RNG of the game, so if you care about score attack stuff I wouldn't take it seriously).

That's really the main gimmick here for this entry into the genre. Right now there's only 1 level (and I'm not really sure what more levels would mean for something like this). There are a few enemies but only 1, besides the boss, is a threat, and I think that's due to either a bug or questionable design. You can basically win 100% of your runs by taking a pistol or katana to start, and just taking every +offensive perk option you see when you level up (and avoid taking the income increasing ones since that means your funds eclipse your levels too fast). 

On the surface that's fine, I like when these games don't require meta upgrades to beat the base difficulty. The thing is, there aren't any meta upgrades, there are just more perks and weapon options to unlock, and a lot of them aren't really good (or they require a lot of other luck getting synergies to be good).

After 3 hours I feel like I've seen what it has to offer, and it's fun enough for 3 bucks, but just know what to expect when you grab it. Since it's EA this could well change but right now the balance of the game makes it pretty stale pretty quickly compared to a lot of these types. I don't mind having a truly short entry though, better in some ways than the ones where you have to repetitively grind something often frustrating 80 times to get an achievement or unlock (looking at you, Army of Ruin)

[b][h1]BloodDome99[/h1][/b]BloodDome99 is a typical bullet-heaven in an 80's arcade style, it doesn't do a whole lot new with the genre, but it also doesn't overstay it's welcome. It's damn cheap and you get your money's worth.

[b][h2]Gameplay[/h2][/b]You kill enemies to gain money and exp, when you level up you spend the money you gained on upgrades, when you reach 300,000$ the final boss spawns and you must kill it and have 300,000$ to win the run. This makes for an interesting dynamic of spending more to delay and prepare for the boss or underspending to rush the boss for a good leaderboard position.

The weapons and perks in the game aren't particularly anything new for the genre, it plays very similar to Neon Sundown or 20 Minutes Till Dawn, particularly in having a movement penalty when auto-shooting.

You unlock more weapons and perks through completing certain tasks, these aren't really shown to you, you just achieve them as you go. It would be better if there was some way to see these. At the end of the run the amount of money you have is the amount of meta-currency you have to spend on buying new stuff from the vending machine, which adds to that strategic sense of when to end your run.

There are multiple arenas and bosses for them with varying attack patterns. There are a handful of challenging difficulty modifiers with a "weight" value, with a seperate leaderboard for every weight on every map, it's a super cool system.

[b][h2]Achievements (26/26)[/h2][/b]The achievements aren't all straightforward as most of them don't tell you what to do, so I recommend my guide.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3106913487 side note: the 130 weight achievement is one hell of a challenge.

[b][h2]Music/sound[/h2][/b]For completing certain tasks you can unlock and buy a variety of music tracks, you can switch between these retro beats in the lobby, so it won't really get repetitive. I like the announcer for the blooddome, they have multiple lines for certain scenarios and it really adds to the game.

[b][h2]Settings/Accessibility[/h2][/b]Unlockable advanced targeting. Twitch integration to allow viewers to vote on level-up choices. Keyboard, mouse and gamepad supported. Only English Language.

[b][h2]TL;DR[/h2][/b]
Short but sweet bullet-heaven in an 80's arcade style for a very low price. Unique gameplay loop with money-management. Variety of unlockable perks. Leaderboards. Achievements need a guide, so use mine!

倒せば倒すほどお金が貰えるがパワーアップを重ねていくと
出費もかさむ…という強くなりたいけどもどかしい！
というシステムが面白いと思う

途中本が販売されていることがあり
それを購入すると今まで入手したパワーアップのうち
ON/OFFが出来るようになるので攻略を考えている人は
余分な武器が出ないように調整も出来る

新しいパークもお金で解放されていくので
失敗してもロビーに一度戻れば自販ガチャがあるので
悔しいが楽しい

シンプルなシステムとアイデアで
別のVSライクとは一線が画したいい作品である
